mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in FEDFUNDS above 5% over two consecutive months signals a tightening monetary regime, which raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in GDPC1 below -2% indicates a significant contraction in aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in UNRATE below 4% for three consecutive months signals weakening labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.3%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in INDPRO above 0.5% for four consecutive months signals accelerating industrial production, which boosts corporate earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly decline in both GDPC1 and HOUST below their respective 12-month moving averages signals deteriorating housing and overall demand, which depresses equity valuations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both below 12-month moving average in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.4%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A positive monthly change in PAYEMS above 0.5% combined with a decline in UNRATE below 4% signals a labor market with rising employment but weakening conditions, which can create uncertainty and lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 0.5% and UNRATE < 4% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.3%) in at least 55% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid increase in FEDFUNDS by more than 1 percentage point within a single month signals an aggressive tightening stance, which sharply increases risk-free rates and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.7%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in RSAFS below its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months signals weakening retail sales momentum, which reduces consumer spending and corporate revenue, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS < 12-month moving average for six consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.
